column.createdHint: PRs this contributor opened in this date range, whatever state they are in now. Merged and Closed unmerged are counted separately and are not carved out of this number, so a row is not expected to add up.
column.mergedHint: PRs merged in this date range, whenever they were opened. This is what github.com reports for the same window, so a PR opened last week and merged today counts here and not under Created.
column.closedUnmergedHint: PRs closed in this date range without ever being merged, whenever they were opened. Counted from each PR's own close time, because GitHub's closed: search filter only ever matches merged PRs.
column.stillOpenHint: Of the PRs opened in this date range, the ones neither merged nor closed as of now. The one column that reads the present rather than the range, and the only one tied to Created; it does not include older PRs still waiting.
column.draftsHint: Of the PRs still open from this date range, the ones GitHub still marks as a draft right now. Always a subset of Still open, never a column beside it.
column.totalHint: Additions plus deletions across the PRs merged in this range.
column.prsHint: How many PRs these line counts come from: everything merged in this date range, whenever it was created. That is a wider set than the Merged column above, which only counts PRs created in the range.
column.title: Title
column.stateHint: Where this PR stands right now: merged, closed without merging, open for review, or open but still a draft.
column.deltaHint: Lines added and removed by this PR. Sorts by total lines touched.
column.timeHint: When the PR was merged, closed, or created - whichever put it in this range.

contributions.title: Contribution activity - @{login}
contributions.publicOnly: Public contributions only. This account's token has the scopes [{scopes}], and without read:user GitHub leaves private activity out of the calendar instead of reporting an error - so a busy year can look empty. Fix it by reconnecting the account under Connectors ("Connect with GitHub" requests read:user), or by replacing the token with one that includes read:user. If it still looks empty afterwards, turn on "Include private contributions on my profile" in your GitHub profile settings.

github.needsAuth: Add a GitHub token (keychain fastdash/github/<label> or the GITHUB_TOKEN env var) and pick organizations
github.orgNotGranted: GitHub won't show this account anything in {org}. The connection has every scope it needs (repo, read:org, read:user), but {org} restricts third-party OAuth apps, and fastdash hasn't been granted access - so GitHub hides the org's repositories from it rather than reporting a permission error. Open {url}, find fastdash, and grant it access to {org} (if you don't own the org, that button sends a request to an owner instead). A personal access token isn't subject to this policy, which is why pasting one works today.
github.orgUnsearchable: GitHub can't search {org} with this account's token. Check the organization name under Connectors, and make sure the token has the repo scope and - if {org} enforces SAML single sign-on - has been authorized for it.
github.noScopes: No organizations set for this account. Add an organization, or author:your-login to track every PR you write, under Connectors.
github.scopesFailed: GitHub can't search {scopes}. Check the name under Connectors - use the org's login, user:login for that account's own repos, or author:login for PRs you wrote anywhere - and that your token is authorized for it.
github.scopesPartial: Excludes {scopes}: GitHub wouldn't search it. The totals below cover the remaining scopes only.
github.truncatedTitle: This date range is wider than GitHub will search
github.truncated: GitHub's search API returns at most {cap} results per query, and {range} matched {total} pull requests. Everything below covers only the {cap} most recent of them, so the counts are lower than the truth. Pick a shorter date range for exact numbers.
github.noAccounts: No GitHub accounts connected yet. Add one in Connectors.
